title: BACKND Base SDK usage patterns (knowhow)
summary: Cross-cutting SDK usage patterns: the BackEnd namespace and Backend singleton, synchronous vs asynchronous vs SendQueue calls, building Param objects, parsing BackendReturnObject (rows, unmarshalling, error checking), inDate semantics, and resolving conflicts with external plugins.
capabilities: explain sync, async, and SendQueue call styles and when each applies
guide Param construction and BackendReturnObject parsing
clarify inDate as the row identifier across features
surface plugin-conflict fixes (proguard, litjson, anti-cheat toolkit)
prerequisites: SDK is initialized before any Backend call
The BackEnd namespace is imported in calling scripts
common_pitfalls: Confusing the BackEnd namespace with the Backend singleton (case-sensitive)
Calling a function via SendQueue when that function does not support it
Reading return values without checking IsSuccess and status/error codes first
verification_required_for: exact return-object field and method names
verification_strategy: Use https://docs.backnd.com plus the source route before presenting exact return-parsing or Param code.
Confirm whether a given function supports SendQueue from its own reference page.
public_notes: These are usage patterns shared across features; per-feature exactness still comes from each feature topic.
Useful before generating any BACKND call code to get call style and return parsing right.
